_doc: THE CARRIAGE LEDGER - adjudicated answers to 'does any Omaha store stock this food?', keyed by commodity id (or 'item:<Item Name>' for an ingredient that has no bid, e.g. Keto Bun). Read through lib\carriage-lib.ps1 by every gate; never read directly. This file holds ONLY verdicts a human or the recipe-hunter-pricer adjudicated from real store evidence. The automatic tier is the live feed (grocery\out\smp-feed.json): a bid with >=1 real store price there is CARRIED without needing a row here, which covers 273 of the 275 bids in live use. This file is for the remainder.
_rule: CARRIED needs store + item + price + as_of. NOT-CARRIED needs all seven Omaha stores recorded as having ANSWERED (state carried|not-carried; blocked/error/unreached do NOT count) plus the terms tried at each - Rule B, identical to grocery\ingredient-queue.ps1. Anything weaker degrades to UNKNOWN at read time, so a hand-edited pardon cannot open the gate. UNKNOWN is an explicit, valid record: it is where the history of a failed search lives.
_why_unknown_matters: Every 'absence' this estate has ever found was a wrong search term, not an empty shelf. doubanjiang was searched as 'chili bean sauce' and returned 237 rows - all Bush's/Mrs. Grimes chili beans and a Kroger hot dog chili sauce. Korean rice cakes were searched as 'rice cakes' and returned 650 rows of Quaker snack cakes, zero tteok. Neither was ever asked the right question. Recording that as UNKNOWN-with-history, rather than NOT-CARRIED, is what makes a future NOT-CARRIED verdict mean something.

ground-sumac.why: Baker's stocks it. CARRIED but UNPRICED: the matcher never lands it in smp-feed.json, which is why musakhan-sumac-chicken falls back to a label: basis. That is a matcher gap (one of the 13 recoverable), NOT a carriage failure, and it must not take the recipe down. Fixing the matcher retires this row automatically - the feed tier will answer instead.
ground-sumac.recheck: Drop this row once ground-sumac appears in smp-feed.json with a store price.

doubanjiang.why: NEVER ESTABLISHED EITHER WAY - the search term is wrong, so silence proves nothing. commodity-search.json searches doubanjiang as 'chili bean sauce', which returns 237 rows across Family Fare, Walmart and Baker's, every one of them a chili BEAN product (Bush's, Mrs. Grimes) or 'Kroger Hot Dog Chili Sauce'. No row in the entire capture corpus contains 'doubanjiang' or 'toban'. Three recipes were unpublished to DRAFT on 2026-08-22 on this basis (ants-climbing-a-tree-pork-noodles, turkey-ants-climbing-a-tree, taiwanese-braised-beef-noodle-bowls); they are recoverable the moment this resolves CARRIED.
terms_never_tried: Lee Kum Kee chili bean sauce
doubanjiang.recheck: Re-capture with the terms above before ANY verdict. If all seven stores answer and none carry it, promote to NOT-CARRIED with per-store evidence.

Baker\u0027s.evidence: Full ladder walked headless via probe-ingredient.ps1. rung1 'golden beets'=0; rung3 'goldenbeets'=0; pre-pass rung 'golden'=25 tiles, all cereal/beer/pizza-crust (Golden Grahams, Golden Road beer) - wrong rung for a 2-word term. I walked the correct head-noun rung 'beets'=25 genuine beet products: Beets Bunch 1 lb, Organic RED Beets .49/lb, Del Monte Sliced, Kroger Whole/Sliced/Shoestring, Aunt Nellie's pickled - every one red or unspecified, none golden/yellow. Synonym rungs also walked: 'gold beets'=1 -> 'goldbeets'=8 all Haribo Goldbears gummy candy; 'yellow beets'=13 all Yellow Tail wine. Beets category is well populated here, so the absence of the golden variety within it is meaningful, not a search-box artifact. No beet commodity appears in audit-search-terms.ps1.

Family Fare.evidence: Full ladder walked headless via probe-ingredient.ps1 (Freshop store_id 6401 Omaha). rung1 'golden beets'=0; rung3 'goldenbeets'=0; pre-pass rung 'golden'=25 tiles all Golden Delicious apples/Twinkies/Coors Banquet/Golden Oreo - wrong rung. Correct head-noun rung 'beets'=13 genuine beet products: Baby RED Beets .49, Our Family Diced/Whole/Sliced Beets 15oz .19, Del Monte Sliced 14.5oz, Aunt Nellie's + Paisley Farm pickled, Mrs Gerrys Beets And Onions - all red or unspecified, none golden/yellow. Synonyms too: 'gold beets'=0 and 'goldbeets'=0 (fell back to 'beets'); 'yellow beets'=0, 'yellowbeets'=0, 'yellow'=25 all bananas/corn/peppers/onions. Populated beets category with no golden variety.

Hy-Vee.evidence: hy-vee.com aisles-online, store 'Omaha #01, NE', searched 'golden beets': '1 - 7 of 7 Results'. All seven adjudicated and rejected as not golden: Green Top Beets Bunch 1 ct $3.99 (red beets), Hy-Vee Sliced Beets 15 oz, Hy-Vee Diced Beets 15 oz, Aunt Nellie's Sweet & Sour Harvard Beets, Aunt Nellie's Sliced Pickled Beets, Aunt Nellie's Whole Pickled Beets, Del Monte Crinkle Cut Pickled Beets. The store clearly stocks fresh beets and canned beets, so the absence of a GOLDEN beet is a meaningful absence rather than a catalogue gap.

Aldi.evidence: aldi.us, In-Store, ALDI - OLA 48 - Omaha. Three rungs, all returning the literal no-results banner with suggestion tiles only: 'golden beets' -> 'No results for golden beets', 'beets' -> 'No results for beets', 'beet' -> 'No results for beet'. Suggestions were ordinary produce (radishes, ginger, carrots, celery, cucumber, red onions). Control terms 'bananas' and 'dill pickles' returned no banner and real results in the same session. Aldi Omaha stocks no beet of any colour, golden included.

Fareway.evidence: shop.fareway.com, In-Store, retailerLocation 531573 Omaha verified. Two rungs, both with the literal banner: 'golden beets' -> 'No results for golden beets' and 'gold beet' -> 'No results for gold beet', each scrolled to a stable 60 tiles. A separate 'beets' query returned 5 genuine hits with NO banner - Fareway Sliced/Whole/Diced Beets 15 oz $1.44, Aunt Nellie's Sliced Pickled Beets, Love Beets Cooked 8.8 oz $4.99 - proving the store does stock beets and that the golden-specific empty is a real absence. Every stocked beet is red, canned or pre-cooked. (An earlier run of this term produced a stale scrape showing dill rows; it was discarded and the query re-run, which is where these banners come from.)

Sam\u0027s Club.evidence: samsclub.com, club 'Omaha Sam's Club' 68144, /search?q=golden beets via __NEXT_DATA__. Sam's returns related-item filler rather than an empty grid, and not one row was a beet in any form: Neuriva brain supplement, Qunol magnesium, Giorgio mushrooms, Premier Protein, VitaCup coffee, canned peaches, whey isolate. The single near-hit is 'Force Factor Total Beets Soft Chews, Acai Berry, 90 ct' - a supplement chew, the documented brand-name trap, not a vegetable. No golden beet.

Walmart.evidence: walmart.com in Brad's Chrome, store 'Omaha L St Supercenter'. Two rungs: 'golden beets' (46 rows) and the widened 'beets', both filtered to fulfillmentType=STORE. The STORE rows are 'Fresh Whole Red Beets Bunch' $2.67, 'Fresh Organic Whole Red Beets, 1 lb Bag' $3.38, and canned red beets (Great Value Sliced $0.78, Libby's Sliced/Cut $1.47, Del Monte Sliced $1.72, Aunt Nellie's Pickled $2.47). Every fresh beet stocked at the Omaha store is RED. No golden or yellow beet at any rung.

Baker\u0027s.evidence: server lane full ladder: 'broccoli rabe'=0, 'broccolirabe'=0, widened rung 'broccoli'=25 returning only ordinary broccoli (crowns, bunches, frozen florets). Broccoli rabe/rapini is a different vegetable (bitter Brassica rapa), not substitutable by a broccoli crown; no rabe/rapini tile at any rung.

Family Fare.evidence: server lane full ladder: 'broccoli rabe'=0, 'broccolirabe'=0, widened rung 'broccoli'=25 - all plain broccoli (crowns, fresh, florets, frozen cuts, beef & broccoli entree). No rabe/rapini. Widening the pool does not widen the ruling.

Hy-Vee.evidence: hy-vee.com aisles-online, store 'Omaha #01, NE'. Rung 1 'broccoli rabe' returned the explicit phrase: broccoli rabe didn't return any results. Please check your spelling and try again. Rung 2 used the correct synonym 'rapini' and returned a single tile which was a SPONSORED placement (Dole Classic Romaine Salad 9 oz) with no result-count line at all, i.e. no genuine result. Two rungs, one of them the proper botanical synonym, both empty.

Aldi.evidence: aldi.us, In-Store, ALDI - OLA 48 - Omaha. Two rungs, both returning the literal banner with suggestion tiles only: 'broccoli rabe' -> No results for broccoli rabe, and the synonym 'rapini' -> No results for rapini. Suggestions were ordinary brassicas - Broccoli Florets 12 oz $2.29, Broccoli Crowns per lb $2.09, Organic Broccoli $3.29, cauliflower crowns, kale, spinach - proving the produce department is stocked and simply has no rabe. Control terms returned real results with no banner in the same session.

Fareway.evidence: shop.fareway.com, In-Store, retailerLocation 531573 Omaha verified. Two rungs, both with the literal banner: 'broccoli rabe' -> No results for broccoli rabe (scrolled to a stable 41 tiles, past the 9-at-a-time lazy-load tell), and 'rapini' -> No results for rapini (13 tiles). Suggestions were ordinary broccoli - crowns $2.48/ea est., Birds Eye and Green Giant frozen florets, Taylor Farms and Pero Family Farms florets, Fareway steamable florets. ONE row deserved a hard look: 'Pero Family Farms Broccoletti 8 oz' $2.99 - REJECTED, because broccoletti/broccolini is baby broccoli, a broccoli-gai lan cross, and NOT rapini/broccoli rabe, which is a turnip relative with the distinct bitter flavour the recipe relies on.

Sam\u0027s Club.evidence: samsclub.com, club 'Omaha Sam's Club' 68144, /search?q=broccoli rabe via __NEXT_DATA__. Sam's returns related-item filler rather than an empty grid; every row was ordinary bulk produce - Taylor Farms Sweet Kale kit, cherry tomatoes, organic green beans, Earthbound Farm organic broccoli florets 2 lbs, Brussels sprouts, baby carrots, russet potatoes, mixed squash, asparagus. No rabe or rapini in a warehouse assortment where a niche bitter green would not be expected.

Walmart.evidence: walmart.com in Brad's Chrome, store 'Omaha L St Supercenter'. Two rungs, 'broccoli rabe' (42 rows) and the synonym 'rapini', both filtered to fulfillmentType=STORE. Real rabe exists on the site - 'Rapini - Broccoli Rabe - 19 oz' $13.90 and a SACLA Friarelli antipasto jar - but both are MARKETPLACE/FC ship-only, not Omaha shelf stock. Every fulfillmentType=STORE row is ordinary broccoli (Fresh Whole Green Broccoli Crowns $1.72, Marketside Fresh Broccoli Florets, Great Value frozen florets/cuts, Fresh Organic Broccoli bunch $3.97) or, on the 'rapini' rung, lettuce and kale. No broccoli rabe stocked at the Omaha store.
